name: Power Ballad for a Tiny Thing
why_it_works: Overblown emotion aimed at a small everyday product is funny, and funny gets shared. Underneath the joke the ballad structure (quiet verse, huge chorus) does real work: the product gets the big moment, so the viewer remembers it as the hero.

hook.pattern: Start whisper-quiet and deadly serious, singing a love song to an ordinary object, then reveal the object.
examples: This is a love song. To my {{product}}.
I wrote a power ballad about {{product}}. No regrets.
You've never heard your {{product}} sung like this.

variables.name: product
variables.description: The product, lowercase, said the way customers say it, 3 syllables or fewer

variables.name: small_moment
variables.description: The tiny daily moment the product shows up in, capitalized, sung in one breath, 8 syllables or fewer
variables.example: Ten p.m., just me and you

variables.name: ballad_line
variables.description: The over-the-top chorus line, capitalized, true to the product, 8 syllables or fewer, no result claims
variables.example: You stay with me while I sleep

variables.name: offer
variables.description: Purchase prompt, starting with a capital or a number, 8 words or fewer
variables.example: 20% off your first jar this week

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Fine-print line from the compliance pack that matches the client's niche, shown small on screen
variables.example: Results vary. These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 moody close-up of a person by a rain-streaked window, single candle light, deadly serious expression, cinematic
Vertical photo of the {{brand}} {{product}} in its everyday spot, soft warm light, romantic framing, shallow depth of field

beats.purpose: one-word pre-chorus with a drum fill
the huge chorus, an octave up: product as hero

visual.prompt: Vertical dramatic slow-motion hero shot of the {{brand}} {{product}} rotating on a pedestal, wind machine, sparks or petals flying, backlit glow, epic music-video style, 9:16
Vertical photo of the same person, now deadpan, holding the {{product}} next to their face, flat daylight, comic contrast

cta: Write your own love song to it: {{offer}} at {{brand}}.

music.feel: retro power ballad, piano and synth pad verse, gated snare and big guitar chorus

craft.technique: Genre-parody structure: quiet verse, octave-up chorus, deadpan tag
craft.notes: Parody the STRUCTURE of a generic retro power ballad, not any real song: whispered verse, one-word pre-chorus ('And then...') over a drum fill, then the same melody sung a full octave up for the chorus, with no key change. Put the key word of {{ballad_line}} on the highest, longest note, aimed at the chorus downbeat. The chorus line uses an internal rhyme or vowel echo (me / sleep). Keep every sung line to one breath, about 8 syllables. The deadpan spoken tag is the comedy turn. Tempo/feel: 70 BPM, piano and synth pad verse, gated snare and big guitar chord on the chorus downbeat. Beat seconds are a guide (about ±1s): the edit is cut to the track, so aim the stresses at the downbeats rather than promising exact bar placement.

do_not: Use a recognizable real ballad melody or a named singer's style
Let the ballad line claim a result the product can't deliver
Spend the clip_hero on anything but the chorus hero shot
compliance: Supplements: no disease or cure claims; structure/function claims need the FDA disclaimer ('These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration...')
Skincare: no medical claims (heals, cures, treats acne/eczema) unless it is a regulated drug product with approved labeling; no before/after without a 'results vary' disclaimer
No unrealistic body or skin images and no shaming language; generated people are labelled as AI content
Show the {{disclosure}} fine print (results vary, plus the FDA line for supplements) on the CTA beat
